main_body: vertical stone column with a wider capital at the top, cylindrical shaft in the middle, and wider base at the bottom
top_band: light grey horizontal top surface of the capital at rows 9-11 bounded by a bright 1px front-edge highlight at row 12
evidence: Reading down the center column: row 8 is the top back outline, rows 9-11 form a 3px light grey horizontal top surface on the capital, and row 12 is a distinct brighter 1px front-edge line (4 rows total for the top band). Rows 13-14 are the vertical front face of the cap, rows 15-16 form a dark overhang/eave shadow onto the shaft, and rows 17-47 are the vertical shaft and base.

style.evidence: Unlike the Beodeul well reference where stone is rendered with individual blocks, speckle, and varied shading, the column shaft (rows 17-39) consists of 23 identical rows of unbroken vertical colour stripes with zero stone grain, cracks, or masonry detail, framed by a harsh near-black outline, and the base is a direct copy-paste of the capital.
